1 \(k \geq 3\) Repeated Measures Location Problem

1.1 Overview

For two-way repeated measures layout, we have \(N = nk\) observations

  • \(X_{i1}, \ldots, X_{ik}\) is \(i\)-th block of data

  • \(n\) is the number of subjects/blocks

  • \(k \geq 3\) is the number of treatments

Note: each subject/block participates in \(k\) treatments (so \(X_{ij}\) and \(X_{ij'}\) are dependent)

1.2 Block-Location-Shift Model

The block-location-shift model assumes that

  • \(F_j(z - \theta - \beta_i - \tau_j) = F_0(z)\) where \(\beta_i\) is the \(i\)-th block effect and \(\tau_j\) is \(j\)-th treatment effect

  • \(X_{ij} = \theta + \beta_i + \tau_j + \epsilon_{ij}\) where the \(\epsilon_{ij}\) are iid with median zero

1.3 Null and Alternative Hypotheses

The null hypothesis assumes that all treatments have the same effect \[ H_{0}: \tau_1 = \tau_2 = \cdots = \tau_k \] and we only have one reasonable alternative: \[ H_{1}: \tau_j \neq \tau_{j'} \ \mbox{for some} \ j,j' \]

2 Methodological Details

2.1 Friedman Statistic

Let \(r_{ij} \in \{1,\ldots,k\}\) denote the rank of \(X_{i1},\ldots,X_{ik}\) within the \(i\)-th block.

Defining the sum and average of the combined ranks for each group \[ R_{j}= \sum_{i=1}^{n} r_{ij} \qquad \mbox{and} \qquad \bar{R}_j = R_{j}/n \] the Friedman test statistic \(S\) is defined as \[ S = \frac{12n}{k(k+1)}\sum_{j=1}^{k} \left(\bar{R}_j - \frac{k+1}{2}\right)^{2} \] where \(\frac{k+1}{2}=(\sum_{i=1}^{n}\sum_{j=1}^{k}r_{ij}/N)\) is average of within-block rankings.

2.2 Null Distribution

Under \(H_0\) all \(M = (k!)^n\) arrangements occur with equal probability.

  • \(n\) independent subjects and \(k\) treatments for each subject

  • Given \(n\) and \(k\), calculate \(S\) for all \(M\) possible outcomes

  • Each outcome has probability \(1/ M\) under \(H_0\)

For \(n = 1\) subject with \(k = 3\) treatments, there are \(M = 6\) arrangements.

Block \(R_1\) \(R_2\) \(R_3\)
\(i\) 1 2 3
\(i\) 1 3 2
\(i\) 2 1 3
\(i\) 2 3 1
\(i\) 3 1 2
\(i\) 3 3 2

2.3 Statistical Inference

2.3.1 Exact Test

One-Sided Test (Greater Than)

  • \(H_{0}: \tau_1 = \tau_2 = \cdots = \tau_k\)   versus   \(H_{1}: \tau_j \neq \tau_{j'} \ \mbox{for some} \ j,j'\)

  • Reject \(H_{0}\) if \(S \geq s_{1-\alpha}\) where \(P(S>s_{1-\alpha})=\alpha\)

  • P-Value: \(p = \frac{1}{M} \sum_{j=1}^{M} I(S_j \geq S_{\mathrm{obs}})\) where \(M = (k!)^n\)

Note: this is the only option because larger values of \(S\) provide more evidence against \(H_0\).

2.3.2 Large Sample Approximation

As \(n \rightarrow \infty\), we have that \(S \sim \chi^{2}_{k-1}\)

  • \(\chi^{2}_{k-1}\) denotes a chi-squared distribution with \(k-1\) df

  • Reject \(H_{0}\) if \(S \geq s_{1-\alpha}^*\) where \(P(\chi^{2}_{k-1} > s_{1-\alpha}^*) = \alpha\)

  • P-Value: calculations from the \(\chi_{k-1}^2\) distribution

2.3.3 Handling Ties

When there are ties, we need to replace \(S\) with \[ S^{*} = \frac{12\sum_{j=1}^{k} \left(R_{j} - \frac{n(k+1)}{2}\right)^{2}}{nk(k+1)-\frac{1}{k-1}\sum_{i=1}^{n}\left[\left(\sum_{j=1}^{g_{i}} t_{ij}^{3}\right) - k\right] } \] where

  • \(g_{i}\) is the number of tied groups in \(i\)-th block

  • \(t_{ij}\) is the size of the \(j\)-th tied group in \(i\)-th block

3 Example

3.1 Data and Problem

3.1.1 Overview of Problem

Example 7.1 from Nonparametric Statistical Methods, 3rd Ed

\(n=22\) baseball players participated in a base-running experiment.

Response variable is the time (in seconds) it takes to run from home plate to 2nd base.

Goal was to compare \(k=3\) methods to round first base:

  • Round out (diamond)

  • Narrow angle (asterisk)

  • Wide angle (solid)

Reproduction of Figure 7.1 from Nonparametric Statistical Methods, 3rd Edition.

3.2.2 Test Statistic

The uncorrected test statistic has the form \[ \begin{split} S &= 22 \left( (53/22 - 2)^2 + (47/22 - 2)^2 + (32/22 - 2)^2 \right) \\ &= 10.63636 \end{split} \]

There are ties in blocks \(i\in\{7,15,17,22\}\) such that \[ t_{i1}=2 \ \ \mbox{and} \ \ t_{i2}=1 \] because there is one tied group of size 2 and one tied group of size 1 for each block \(\Longrightarrow\) \((\sum_{j=1}^{g_{i}} t_{ij}^{3}) - k = (2^3+1^3)-3=6\) for each block.

The corrected test statistic value is \[ \begin{split} S^* &= \frac{12 \left[ (53-44)^{2} + (47-44)^{2} + (32-44)^{2} \right]}{22(3)(4) - (1/2)(6)(4) }\\ &= \frac{(53-44)^{2} + (47-44)^{2} + (32-44)^{2}}{21}\\ &= 11.14286 \end{split} \]

3.3 Using R

3.3.1 Input Data

Load Data:

widetime <- matrix(c(5.40, 5.50, 5.55,
                     5.85, 5.70, 5.75,
                     5.20, 5.60, 5.50,
                     5.55, 5.50, 5.40,
                     5.90, 5.85, 5.70,
                     5.45, 5.55, 5.60,
                     5.40, 5.40, 5.35,
                     5.45, 5.50, 5.35,
                     5.25, 5.15, 5.00,
                     5.85, 5.80, 5.70,
                     5.25, 5.20, 5.10,
                     5.65, 5.55, 5.45,
                     5.60, 5.35, 5.45,
                     5.05, 5.00, 4.95,
                     5.50, 5.50, 5.40,
                     5.45, 5.55, 5.50,
                     5.55, 5.55, 5.35,
                     5.45, 5.50, 5.55,
                     5.50, 5.45, 5.25,
                     5.65, 5.60, 5.40,
                     5.70, 5.65, 5.55,
                     6.30, 6.30, 6.25),
                   ncol = 3, byrow = TRUE)

Long version of data

longtime <- data.frame(time = c(widetime),
                       block = rep(1:nrow(widetime), times = ncol(widetime)),
                       group = rep(1:ncol(widetime), each = nrow(widetime)))
head(longtime)
##   time block group
## 1 5.40     1     1
## 2 5.85     2     1
## 3 5.20     3     1
## 4 5.55     4     1
## 5 5.90     5     1
## 6 5.45     6     1

Note: the nptest package requires vectorized data with group running faster than block (so that widetime can be reconstructed as matrix(longtime, nblocks, ngroups)).

3.3.2 Friedman Rank Sum Test (stats package)

Friedman Rank Sum Test using stats package:

friedman.test(widetime)
## 
##  Friedman rank sum test
## 
## data:  widetime
## Friedman chi-squared = 11.143, df = 2, p-value = 0.003805

3.3.3 Friedman Rank Sum Test (nptest package)

Friedman Rank Sum Test using nptest package:

library(nptest)
## Package 'nptest' version 1.2
## Type 'citation("nptest")' to cite this package.
set.seed(1)
mod <- np.aov.test(longtime$time, longtime$group, longtime$block, 
                   median.test = TRUE, var.equal = TRUE)
mod
## 
## Friedman ANOVA Test (Equal Variances)
## Number of Groups: 3     Number of Blocks: 22 
## H = 10.6364,  p-value = 0.0036
plot(mod)

Note: the nptest package returns the uncorrected test statistic \(S\) (instead of \(S^*\)).
